daily.title: India–UAE DTAA Tie-Breaker Rules: Tax Residency, Permanent Home & Vital Interests
daily.summary: Understand India–UAE DTAA tie-breaker rules, the 183-day condition, permanent home, vital interests, habitual abode, POEM and TRC requirements. An Indian entrepreneur may live in Dubai, operate a UAE company and hold a UAE Tax Residency Certificate, yet still satisfy the Indian domestic test for tax residence. When both countries have a valid residence claim, counting days alone may not settle the final treaty position. Article 4 of the India–UAE Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement contains tie-breaker rules for such cases. These rules determine the country in which a dual-resident individual will be treated as resident for applying the treaty.
